Since \(PW \parallel QX\), the segment \(UV\) is parallel to \(ST\).

At \(U\),  
\[
\angle SUV = 120^\circ.
\]
Because \(UV \parallel ST\), the angle between \(SU\) and \(ST\) is supplementary:
\[
\angle UST = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ.
\]
Thus in triangle \(RST\),
\[
\angle RST = 60^\circ.
\]

At \(T\),  
\[
\angle VTX = 112^\circ.
\]
Since \(TX\) and \(TS\) are opposite rays,
\[
\angle VTS = 180^\circ - 112^\circ = 68^\circ.
\]
Because \(R\) lies on ray \(TV\), we have
\[
\angle RTS = 68^\circ.
\]

Now in triangle \(RST\),
\[
\angle URV = \angle SRT = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 68^\circ = 52^\circ.
\]

The answer is \(52^\circ\).
